# Problem 1 (Central Limit Theorem for two proportions)
Let $X_1\sim \text{Bin}(n_1, \theta_1)$ and $X_2\sim \text{Bin}(n_2,\theta_2)$
be two independent random variables. For each $(n_1,n_2)\in\{(15,20),(30,40), (50,80)\}$,
and each $(\theta_1,\theta_2)\in\{(0.1, 0.2),(0.5,0.5),(0.8,0.9)\}$ compute via
simulation the distribution of the Z statistic (the two sample version of that in slide~111)
$$
Z = \frac{(\hat \theta_1 - \hat \theta_2) - (\theta_1-\theta_2)}{
\sqrt{\frac{\hat\theta_1(1-\hat\theta_1)}{n_1}+\frac{\hat\theta_2(1-\hat\theta_2)}{n_2}}},
$$
where $\hat \theta_i = X_i/n_i$. Using $N = 10^5$ simulations and random seed equal
to 21:
(i) Compare the histogram of $Z$ with that of the $N(0,1)$. 
(ii) Argue why the histogram should behave as a standard normal distribution 
as $n_1$ and $n_2$ are both large.
(iii) With the estimated standard error in the denominator, \(Z\) can be 
undefined when both sample proportions are 0 or 1. Report how often that 
occurs and how did you handle it.

# Problem 2 (The Empirical Distribution Function)

distribution

 (a)  Read about the empirical distribution function (eCDF, written $\hat F$) at https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Empirical_distribution_function.
 (b)  Then read Chapter6.pdf. 
 (c)  Choose one of the cases illustrated in Problem 1 and draw the 
 empirical distribution function of Z along with the distribution function of $N(0,1)$ 
 (d)  Explain why the empirical distribution function is preferable to the histogram for comparing the distribution of \(Z\) with the \(N(0,1)\) distribution. Explain how the histogram’s dependence on binning affects the comparison.

# Problem 3 (More on the power of a test)

(a) Let 3.97, 3.39, 3.08, 4.11, 4.83, 3.80, 4.51, 3.60, 4.53, 3.60, 4.87, be an observed
sample of CO levels (in ppm) measured on a synthetic air sample. Assume the data are independent realisations from a normal distribution with 
random measurement error having variance $\sigma_0=0.5\,$ (in ppm$^2$). Test 
$H_0:\mu\leq 3.7$ against a proper alternative at the significance level
$\alpha=0.10$. Conclude using both the p-value and the acceptance region.

(b) While keeping $H_0:\mu\leq 3.7$, assume $H_1$ is true with $\mu=3.9$. What is the
amount the type II error? Illustrate the type II error by means of a diagram.

(c) While keeping $H_0:\mu\leq 3.7$, define an R function that given the 
sample size $n$, the value of 
$\mu$ under the alternative hypothesis and $\alpha=0.10$, computes the type II 
error ($\beta$) of the test. Draw this function for $n=2:50$ on the $x$-axis when: (i) $\mu=3.9$, (ii) $\mu=4.0$ and (iii) $\mu=4.1$. Comment the results.

(d) While keeping $H_0:\mu\leq 3.7$, define an R function that, with $n=20$, and $\mu=3.95$, 
takes as input $\beta$ and outputs $\alpha$. Draw the function on a regular
grid of $\beta \in (0,0.5]$.
